title: Should Have: The Oil Boom and Its End

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *Deberías haber llamado* and regrets and reproaches from B2 Unit 10: the modal stays in the conditional and *haber* + past participle carries the past (*Deberías haber llamado*, *Me arrepiento de haber dicho eso*). Economists use the same pattern to look back at the years of high oil prices and say what the country should have done. Remember that these are opinions of people, not facts.

sections.title: Looking back
rows: We should have saved more. (regret about ourselves)
El país debería haber ahorrado más dinero.
The country should have saved more money. (reproach)
Tendrían que haber usado el dinero para otras industrias.
They should have used the money for other industries.
Me arrepiento de no haber ahorrado más.
I regret not having saved more.

items.spanish: Según varios economistas, el país debería haber ahorrado más en los años de precios altos.
items.english: According to several economists, the country should have saved more in the years of high prices.

items.spanish: Deberían haber usado el dinero para otras industrias, dicen algunos analistas.
items.english: They should have used the money for other industries, say some analysts.

items.spanish: Me arrepiento de no haber ahorrado más.
items.english: I regret not having saved more.

sections.content: Compare *Deberíamos ahorrar más* (advice about now) with *Deberíamos haber ahorrado más* (a reproach about the past). Only *haber* carries the past: the modal stays *debería*, and the participle never changes: *haber ahorrado*. When you report a view like this, say whose it is.
